episodes.212466: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of June 2 across central and north central South Dakota. The storms produced golf ball-sized hail five miles southwest of the Counselor Creek Recreation Area and quarter-sized hail two miles north of Hoven. The COOP observer near Artas recorded an 80 mph wind gust on a personal weather station, which damaged a swing set and knocked a camper off its cinderblocks. Additionally, the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station nine miles north-northwest of Vivian recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
episodes.212498: A slow moving upper level disturbance over northern Mexico and the Desert Southwest combined with moist surface southeast flow resulting in thunderstorm development across central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours. Some storms resulted in severe hail at Chacon, severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Sumner Lake and Endee on June 2nd and some burn scar flash flooding in Ruidoso on June 3rd.
episodes.212564: An isolated strong storm moved across north central South Dakota during the late morning of June 3rd. The public submitted reports of quarter-sized hail three miles northeast of Green Grass and two miles northeast of White Horse.
episodes.212565: Several clusters of severe thunderstorms tracked across portions of central and northeast South Dakota during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 3, generating high winds, large hail, and heavy rainfall.  ||One cluster tracked along the North Dakota border, where a personal weather station in Frederick recorded a peak wind gust of 84 mph. These high winds destroyed the football field scoreboard and a storage shed in Frederick, knocked down trees and a radio tower, downed power lines in Hecla, and snapped power poles and flipped an irrigation pivot six miles north of Britton. The city of Britton lost electrical power. Three additional weather stations in Marshall County clocked wind gusts in excess of 60 mph. ||A second storm cluster moved out of eastern South Dakota into the southern Glacial Lakes region. Quarter-sized hail occurred at several locations. Heavy rainfall topping out at 4.40 inches in Clear Lake resulted in water six inches deep running over roads and caused a creek near the golf course to overflow its banks. Across central South Dakota, storms produced hail ranging from penny to golf ball size south of Interstate 90.
episodes.212704: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms form just east of I-25 dropping up to one inch diameter hail from Denver to Greeley.
episodes.212850: Widespread thunderstorms initially developed across the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico on the afternoon of the second, fueled by abundant moisture and aided by a mid-level disturbance moving across the region. The slow-moving thunderstorms ingested deep and rich moisture, leading to widespread moderate to heavy rainfall. The large expanse of rain gradually built eastward across the Texas/New Mexico state line and into the western South Plains and Texas Panhandle through the evening hours. Additional storm development blossomed along a low-level boundary over parts of the central and southeastern South Plains late in the evening, before being overtaken by the initial activity to the west early in the morning on the third. Relatively weak vertical wind shear and modest instability limited overall storm strength but produced torrential rainfall. Where the heaviest rain fell, portions of Farm to Market Road 212 and US Highway 380 in eastern and northeastern Lynn County were flooded. Flooding was also observed in and around Brownfield (Terry County), as well over northwestern portions of Cochran County, including in some locations along Farm to Market Road 596 northwest of Morton (Cochran County).
episodes.213270: During the afternoon and evening of June 2, thunderstorm development was initiated by a weak backdoor cold front moving in from the northeast. The resulting activity was primarily concentrated within and surrounding the DFW Metroplex, leading to instances of marginally severe hail and strong to severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.213278: From June 2-4, 2026, a series of disturbances tracking across the region within broad zonal flow set off several rounds of thunderstorms to the region. A slow-moving front on June 2 set off the first round of thunderstorms, producing widespread heavy rain and localized flash flooding. The most significant impacts occurred in Oglala and surrounding communities, where 6 to 7 inches of rain fell in a short period, causing streets and ditches to fill extremely quickly. Some storms also produced large hail and strong winds. Some storms also produced large hail and strong winds.||June 3 brought another round of storms as a disturbance moved across the Northern Plains. Clearing over Wyoming and the Black Hills allowed storms to redevelop along a boundary across southern South Dakota. Several became supercells, including the storm that produced the rain-wrapped Ideal tornado in Tripp County. The tornado mainly affected agricultural land but damaged multiple outbuildings and caused additional RFD���related damage to a nearby modular home.||On June 4, the severe threat was more limited. Lower dewpoints over Wyoming and a strong cap over the Black Hills and western South Dakota kept storm coverage down, though a few storms still became severe with larger hail and strong wind gusts. A landspout also occurred in northeast Wyoming with one of the isolated storms.
episodes.213744: Showers and thunderstorms affected the combined Panhandles each afternoon and evening in the early parts of June. With enough moisture, instability and sources to provide atmospheric lift, these storms were able to become severe each day and bring large hail to the region. A few instances of damaging winds and flooding also occurred.
episodes.213790: Showers and thunderstorms initially developed off the higher terrain in west Texas and southeast New Mexico during the afternoon of June 2nd. Later that evening, storms coalesced into a line behind an outflow boundary, which moved out of southeast New Mexico and into the Permian Basin. Severe winds accompanied this line as it moved across SE New Mexico and the western Basin. Heavy rainfall also led to instances of flash flooding through the morning of the 3rd before the line fully dissipated.
episodes.213791: Showers and thunderstorms initially developed off the higher terrain in west Texas and southeast New Mexico during the afternoon of June 2nd. Later that evening, storms coalesced into a line behind an outflow boundary, which moved out of southeast New Mexico and into the Permian Basin. Severe winds accompanied this line as it moved across SE New Mexico and the western Basin. Heavy rainfall also led to instances of flash flooding through the morning of the 3rd before the line fully dissipated.
episodes.213903: Scattered thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 2nd, the strongest of which produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.213973: As an upper level low moved through the region, severe thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front that moved through North Dakota. Scattered showers and non-severe thunderstorms were ongoing during the morning before increasing in strength throughout the afternoon. A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved through parts of north central North Dakota, including the Turtle Mountains area, before additional storms developed to the south in the James River Valley area. |The most significant damage occurred approximately 4 miles northeast of Belcourt. Multiple buildings were damaged at a collection of properties in this area. A garage on the southwest side of the damage area lost a section of its roof that video and drone footage show was blown northeast across the property. The other main building with damage is a residential home at the center property that lost a significant portion of its roof ripped off. On the north and east side of this property, there were multiple hardwood trees damaged, some snapped about halfway down, but all generally extending to the northeast. A utility truck was parked at the center property and was facing south when the storm came through. A two by four plank of wood went through the windshield and both occupants of the truck had minor injuries. At the eastern property in this group, a shed collapsed and was blown into the edge of a wooded area to the northeast. Drone footage shows numerous trees damaged in this wooded area, extending a few hundred feet northeast of the buildings on the property. Winds were estimated at 95 mph. To the northeast, there was another property with approximately 15 to 20 oak trees that were damaged. |The other main area of damage occurred in Stutsman County, one mile west of Spiritwood. A 200 foot by 60 foot barn was blown over and dismantled. Based on photo and satellite imagery, barn was oriented west-east with 3 doors facing south. The storm was moving from south to north, which would be a favorable direction to funnel wind into the broad side of the barn with multiple doors, helping the barn collapse and push pieces into the tree row directly to the north. This is consistent with wind speeds of around 85 mph.|The highest measured wind gust was 62 mph near Zeeland in Mcintosh County and near Pettibone in Kidder County. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized, west of Belcourt in Rolette County.
episodes.214341: Scattered multi-cell thunderstorms developed near the 100th meridian west during the afternoon and evening of the 3rd. The strongest thunderstorms produced strong-severe winds associated with downbursts.
episodes.214506: A trough axis extending from the eastern Great Lakes into the Mid-Atlantic states and a ridge centered over the central and southern Plains placed the forecast area directly between both features.  A weak front approached the area from the north.   This front was the initial focal point for convective activity to begin developing in the afternoon hours.  This activity capitalized on a warm, moist, and unstable environment to produce slow moving strong thunderstorms in the Baton Rouge area.  These storms produce isolated flash flooding and severe wind gusts.
episodes.214598: A deep upper-level trough moved along the international border with a strengthening southerly flow of moisture and instability into southeast South Dakota. With the terminus of the transport near the mid-James River Valley, isolated storms developed by very late afternoon with strong updrafts and large hail up to ping-pong ball size. A more linear system developed along the dry line in central South Dakota during the early evening and produced damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph near and south of Interstate 90.
episodes.214848: Severe thunderstorms occurs from late morning through the evening hours across the Devils Lake Basin and northeast North Dakota. Large hail to the size of golf balls was reported, and severe winds to 73 mph were measured.
episodes.214849: A severe thunderstorm developed northwest of Grand Forks, ND near Mekinock, ND during the late afternoon.
episodes.215087: An inverted trough of low pressure moved into Texas from the Gulf of Mexico and generated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail over South-Central Texas.
episodes.215150: During the mid to late afternoon hours on the 3rd, scattered to numerous thunderstorms moved north to northeast across western and northwest Kansas, ahead of an upper level disturbance approaching from the southwest. Wind gusts estimated at 60 mph occurred in Graham county, which was the only severe weather report received throughout this event.
episodes.215589: Southeast surface flow helped bring in some modest moisture to the Rio Grande Valley near El Paso with south-southwest flow aloft resulting in wind shear across the area. A severe storm was able to develop in northeast El Paso and hail up to 1 inch in diameter was reported.
episodes.215611: Diurnal convection developed early in the month of June. Isolated severe storms also developed.
episodes.215828: Strong thunderstorms moved down the Space and Treasure Coasts in the morning.
episodes.215831: A morning storm produced a severe wind gust along the coast.
episodes.215924: South Florida was in the warm sector of a surface frontal system with a broad area of high pressure over the eastern United States. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours over Southeast Florida and the adjacent waters.
episodes.215925: South Florida was in the warm sector of a surface frontal system with a broad area of high pressure over the eastern United States. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours over Southeast Florida and the adjacent waters.
episodes.216026: An isolated waterspout was observed in association with a convective rain shower.  An upper-level trough of low pressure was located over the Gulf, with a mid latitude trough over the southeastern United States.
episodes.216096: An isolated thunderstorm occurred over far southeast Montana, producing hail up to 3 inches in diameter.

Thunderstorms repeatedly developed over the same areas on June 2, 2026 leading to flash flooding, that turned into pluvial flooding. Runoff from an estimated 5 to 7 inches of rain caused considerable damage in Oglala. Seven buildings were destroyed, 24 buildings had major damage, and 10 other structures reported minor damager. Highway 18 and BIA 41 were also inundated.
The ASOS at Muskogee-Davis Regional Airport measured thunderstorm wind gusts to 62 mph.

An NWS storm survey revealed extensive flooding in eastern Lynn County from heavy rainfall late on the third into the early morning hours of the fourth. The most widespread flooding occurred along Farm to Market Road 212 north of US Highway 380. Standing water still covered parts of the roadway the next morning. There also existed further evidence that water covered a greater portion of the roadway by the mud left behind as the water receded. Additional flooding occurred along US Highway 380 between Farm to Market 212 and Tahoka.

An NWS storm survey revealed extensive flooding in and around Brownfield and along US Highway 385 and US Highway 62/82 north of Brownfield. Standing water was still present on area roadways the morning after the event.

An NWS storm survey revealed extensive flooding along Farm to Market 596 in northwestern Cochran County. Numerous locations along this road showed evidence of previous water over the roadway. Standing water still existed on portions of the road the next morning.

Public reports 3 or 4 stalled out cars on I-20 westbound between FM1788 and Loop 338 exits heading into Odessa. Video of flash flooding was also shared on social media. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar and from the time of the initial reports. The cost of damages is also estimated.
